title: Dead of Ninety-Two and Ninety-Three
text:
Dead of Ninety-two and Ninety-three,

who, pale from the kiss freedom gives,

calmly shattered with your clogs the yoke

that weighs upon the soul and brow of the world;


Ecstatic men, great in the storm,

you whose love leapt wrapped in rags,

soldiers whom Death, noble Lover, sowed

through the ancient furrows to regenerate them;


whose blood washed sullied grandeur clean.

Dead there at Valmy, at Fleurus, in Italy,

million Christs, Dead, with gentle, dark eyes;


sleep with the Republic, while we go

bent beneath kings as beneath a lash.

—For it is the Cassagnacs who remember you now.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Rimbaud's revolutionary apostrophe and the bitter final turn toward reactionary commemoration.

title: Song from the Aquarium
text:
I drained the cup to the bottom. That is, I was seduced.

I was a child, and they loved me.

The world despaired, for I remained pure. She

rolled on the floor before me, with tender limbs

and an alluring backside. I stood firm.

To calm her, when she grew too excited, I lay with her

and became impure.

Sin satisfied me. Philosophy helped me at dawn,

when I kept watch. I became what they wanted.

For a long time I looked upward and thought the sky was

sad above me. But I saw it was indifferent to it.

It loved itself.

Now it has been a long time since I drowned. I lie swollen on

the bottom.

The fish live inside me. The sea is running out.
editorial_note: The translation follows the likely idiom of 'copa' in the opening while preserving the aquarium speaker's drowned self-accusation.

title: The Light Is Cold
text:
The light of memory is cold

what was barely glimpsed shines

with insistence

turns, seeking the bottle shard

or the rain puddle


behind any door that opens

is the moon

so large and flat

so out of place

as if it were a painting

oil on paper

hardened by time


thus they fell into the mind

forms and colors

coincidences

chance that knots shadows

upheavals in the black cauldron

where in bubbling surges

joy and dread are cooked


the plaster of a sky grows

wounded a thousand times

whitened a thousand times

the world is erased and written

again

to the last breath


only this

apparent eternity

wretched splinter of light in

the entrail

of the animal

that barely was
editorial_note: The translation keeps Varela's spare syntax and the memory image as a cold splinter inside a nearly vanished animal.

title: In Castilian
text:
Here you have my voice

raised against the heaven of absurd gods,

my voice stoning the doors of death

with songs that are hard truths like fists.


He died long ago, the day before yesterday. He already stinks.

Here you have my voice setting sail toward the future.

Quickening its step through the ruins,

beautiful as a voyage around the world.


I have suffered much: in this time, all of us

have suffered much.

I raise a cup of joy in my hands,

standing against the twilight.


Erase him. We will forge peace, peace, peace,

by force of caresses, by pure punches.

Here I leave you my voice written in Castilian.

Spain, do not forget that we have suffered together.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Otero's public, combative voice and the closing address to Spain through shared suffering.

title: Equestrian Cat
text:
Which of the two, my tiger, whom do they celebrate,

the edges of dust, the inhabited lances

that flash insurgent windows

in the solemn night of the proclamation?


Whom do the eyes in the combed grass watch?

For whom the flattering smile

in the secret shadows of the square

or the hungry memory of children?


Which of the two exhibits, which submits?

Or perhaps the admirable thing is to be the

extraordinary beast that displays the one who tames it

and enslaves the civil claw that holds it?


Well then, in case it were in your honor,

dance.


Rise on your powerful hindquarters,

offer your golden forehead to the stars,

arch the broad hand

and remain still.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Barral's question of display versus domination in the poised, monumental animal pose.
